Subject: More interpretations of lsb-test-perl results


Hi again,

I've got some more distribution results which I'm trying to align with 
what we ended up with in terms of a spec for Perl in LSB.

If I recall correctly, we decided that all core modules shall be present. 
I remember struggling with DB_File, NDBM_File, ODBM_File for an LSB 
compliant build as these libs are not yet part of LSB, although I was 
eventually able to get them built using static libs.

http://www.linux-foundation.org/~stewb/lsb-perl/perlspec/requiredmodules.html

It turns out some distributions do not ship these, so we see failures 
like:

/ext/NDBM_File/t/ndbm.t|TC 388 FAIL
/ext/ODBM_File/t/odbm.t|TC 319 FAIL
/lib/Memoize/t/tie_ndbm.t|TC 849 FAIL

/ext/DB_File/t/db-btree.t|TC 419 FAIL
/ext/DB_File/t/db-hash.t|TC 418 FAIL
/ext/DB_File/t/db-recno.t|TC 420 FAIL
/ext/ODBM_File/t/odbm.t|TC 319 FAIL

(this is tjreport output from the test journal, but you get the picture)

Running the single tests identify that the modules are not present.

So... do we treat these as failures, or do these particular modules 
qualify for some special treatment? If it's agreed that these could be 
optional, I could report them as a FIP (further information provided), 
rather than a FAIL, and tag them as optional in the LSB spec.
 
Secondly, I've got a distribution that ships a newer CGI.pm from CPAN, 
rather than the perl-5.8.8 version. For the redirect tests, it returns 
"302 Found", rather than "302 Moved". Would it be appropriate to accept 
either result here?

I've got a few other discrepencies from some other distros, but I need to 
work through them a bit before I bring them to the list, to make sure it's 
not a test environment issue.

Thanks,
-- 
Stew Benedict
The Linux Foundation
